items.gloss: object pronouns after prepositions; 'and I' here is hypercorrection

items.term: pronoun case in compound subjects: He and I went (not me and him)
items.gloss: subject pronouns in subjects; 'me and him' is very informal

items.term: compound adjective with a number: a ten-minute walk
items.gloss: number + singular noun, hyphenated, before another noun

items.term: every other / every few: every other day
items.gloss: every other = alternate ones; every few + plural = at short intervals

items.term: quite a few / quite a bit (= many / much)
items.gloss: despite few and bit, it means a fairly large amount

items.term: a couple + plural without of (US informal): a couple weeks
items.gloss: American speech often drops of after a couple

items.term: as many as / as much as + number
items.gloss: stresses that a number or amount is surprisingly large

items.term: much in affirmative sentences: There is much to do
items.gloss: positive much sounds formal; speech prefers a lot of

items.term: generic the + singular: The smartphone changed …
items.gloss: the + singular noun for a whole class, often inventions or species

items.term: the + adjective: the rich, the unemployed
items.gloss: a group of people; takes a plural verb

items.term: a / an with an uncountable + adjective: a good education
items.gloss: a or an when an adjective or of-phrase describes a kind

items.term: countable and uncountable senses: experience vs. an experience
items.gloss: the meaning changes: general skill vs. a single event

items.term: none of + singular or plural verb
items.gloss: both are correct; the singular is more formal

items.term: each / every + singular verb: Each of them has …
items.gloss: each and every take a singular verb, even with of + plural

items.term: neither of + plural noun: Neither of them is / are
items.gloss: a singular verb is formal; a plural verb is common in speech

items.term: either … or / neither … nor agreement
items.gloss: the verb agrees with the closer of the two subjects

items.term: data and media as singular (US)
items.gloss: 'data is' in most American usage; 'data are' in formal science

items.term: classical plurals: criteria, phenomena, hypotheses
items.gloss: singular criterion, phenomenon, hypothesis; avoid 'a criteria'

items.term: plural-looking singulars: news, politics, economics
items.gloss: words ending in -s that take a singular verb

items.term: amounts as singular: Ten dollars is …
items.gloss: money, time and distance seen as one amount take a singular verb

items.term: along with / as well as: the verb agrees with the first subject
items.gloss: added phrases do not make the subject plural

items.term: the majority of + plural verb
items.gloss: the verb follows the noun after of; 'the majority' alone can be singular

items.term: percentages and fractions: 60% of people are …
items.gloss: the verb agrees with the noun after of

items.term: a great deal of vs. a great many
items.gloss: a great deal of + uncountable; a great many + plural

items.term: few vs. a few
items.gloss: few = not many (negative); a few = some (positive)

items.term: little vs. a little
items.gloss: little = not much (negative); a little = some (positive)

items.term: whom in formal English: to whom, for whom
items.gloss: object form; needed after prepositions in formal writing

items.term: whose for things: a company whose profits …
items.gloss: whose can refer to things, not only to people

items.term: all vs. whole: the whole day / all day
items.gloss: whole with singular countable nouns; all with uncountables and plurals

items.term: hyphenated compound adjectives: a well-known author / she is well known
items.gloss: hyphen before a noun; usually no hyphen after the verb

items.term: noun + noun vs. 's vs. of: the car door, the company's success
items.gloss: noun modifier for types; 's for owners; of for parts

items.term: double possessive: a friend of mine
items.gloss: of + possessive for one of several

items.term: time possessive: a week's notice, two years' experience
items.gloss: 's or s' to express a length of time

items.term: than me vs. than I (am)
items.gloss: 'than me' is normal; 'than I am' is careful style

items.term: misused myself: Contact John or myself
items.gloss: use me unless the subject is also I

items.term: the with geographic names: the Netherlands, the Alps
items.gloss: the with plural names, rivers, mountain ranges and some countries

items.term: institution nouns: in the hospital (US), go to college
items.gloss: American English: the with hospital; college with no article

items.term: adjective + a + noun after so / too / how: too big a risk
items.gloss: so, too, as or how + adjective + a + noun

items.term: quite a + noun: That's quite a story
items.gloss: a remarkable or unusual example of something

items.term: kind of / sort of agreement: these kinds of things
items.gloss: this kind of / these kinds of; avoid 'these kind of' in writing

items.term: any (= no matter which): Any student can …
items.gloss: stressed any means every one, without exception

items.term: all but (= almost): all but impossible
items.gloss: all but + adjective = almost; all but one = all except one

items.term: no fewer than / no less than
items.gloss: stresses that a number is surprisingly large

items.term: another + number + plural: another two weeks
items.gloss: another before a number and a plural noun means 'more'

items.term: not all vs. all … not: Not all experts agree
items.gloss: 'not all' is clear; 'all … not' can be ambiguous

items.term: authorial we in papers: In this paper, we show …
items.gloss: we for the authors, even one author, in research writing

items.term: one of the … who + plural verb
items.gloss: the verb agrees with the plural noun: one of those who are

items.term: group possessive: John and Mary's house
items.gloss: one 's for shared ownership; 's on each for separate ownership

items.term: what little / what few: what little time we have
items.gloss: the small amount that there is, all of it
